plain_language: Apple rebuilt its voice assistant using a giant Google AI model. Small requests run on your phone; heavier ones go to a private cloud. You can also choose which AI assistant answers your questions.
findings:
Today's cycle is dominated by a single event with unusual gravitational pull: Apple's WWDC keynote on June 8, Tim Cook's last as CEO, where the iPhone maker rebuilt Siri on a custom roughly 1.2-trillion-parameter Google Gemini model - about eight times larger than the biggest cloud model Apple had built in-house - under a multi-year deal reported around $1 billion a year, with analyst estimates of total value up to $5 billion. After years of failing to ship a competitive in-house assistant, the most vertically integrated device maker outsourced the intelligence layer of its flagship AI feature to the same company that already pays it to be the default search engine - a bet that owning two billion devices and the user gateway matters more than owning the best model. Every validation row today threads back to this one keynote, an unusually concentrated cycle after a light weekend.

The single highest-coherence support is the revived alliance-regime row: the Anthropic-AWS-pact-locks-5-pole-hyperscaler-lab-regime prediction (April 21) catches a major new bilateral device-maker-to-frontier-lab tie at relevance 4, densifying the assistant tier into named lab pairings rather than fragmentation. The honest brake that keeps it from full coherence is mechanism: Apple is a device maker, not a hyperscaler, licensing a model to run behind its own Private Cloud Compute topology rather than entering the exclusive hardware-codesigned cloud pact (Trainium- or TPU-class) the original 5-pole framing centered on. The same keynote also revives the closed-weight-frontier-crystallizes prediction (April 21) at relevance 3: that even a firm with Apple's resources concluded its in-house effort had fallen a generation behind and chose to rent a proprietary closed frontier model is a clean directional read that the closed frontier is pulling away from what self-built models can match, though it does not speak to that prediction's specific falsifiable open-weights-ceiling mechanism around the 35B-A3B class.

The developer-facing half of the keynote feeds the local-and-agent surface rows. Apple's Foundation Models framework now exposes a roughly 3-billion-parameter on-device model to developers for tool-calling and guided (structured) generation with no per-call charge since the model runs locally, while deeper App Intents lets the new assistant chain multi-step tasks across third-party apps. That delivers half of the on-device-LLM-silicon-ships-deskside-plus-sandbox-runtime prediction (June 1) - which named Apple's M-series plus Core ML / MLX heading into WWDC as a peer expected to publish on-device-LLM specs paired with an OS-sandbox runtime - at relevance 3: the on-device-model-exposure side landed, but the sandbox-runtime-at-agent-invocation-granularity side is explicitly deferred to the detailed API sessions running June 9-12, and this is a consumer-class model rather than the 1-PFLOP deskside-silicon floor the prediction quantifies. The same developer surface feeds the open-agent-harness-powers-a-second-vendor's-first-party-agent prediction (June 4) at relevance 3, with the important qualifier that Apple is partly a counter-instance: it built its agent surface on its own first-party frameworks (App Intents plus Foundation Models) rather than embedding an open-source harness, so the open-harness-specific mechanism is unconfirmed; where it leans toward the thesis is the model layer, since the system assistant became a user-selectable slot (Siri, Gemini, ChatGPT, with Anthropic's Claude tested).

The cross-stream pattern is that one keynote simultaneously instantiates a vendor-alliance story (a device maker pairing off with a frontier lab), a market-structure story (renting rather than building the frontier), a local-compute story (a free on-device model exposed to developers), and an agent-surface story (the largest consumer device base becoming addressable in two directions at once). The standing AI-event calendar carries the only non-Apple thread - WWDC now, Databricks June 15-18, the AI Engineer World's Fair June 28-July 2, the Confidential Computing Summit June 23-24 on attested inference, AMD's Advancing AI in July for Instinct MI400 / MI455X, and the Black Hat / DEF CON / Zenity agentic-security track - and it touches the dormant accelerator and security rows only as forward scheduling. As ever, each landing the predictions actually name - a hardware-codesigned exclusive cloud pact, an open-weights ceiling, a published sandbox-runtime entitlement model, an open harness powering a second vendor's first-party agent - is gestured toward by today's evidence rather than delivered.
relation_to_my_preds:
The user's first standing prediction (malicious local LLM as malware + zero-trust as fundamental safeguard) gets only a partial-substrate touch this cycle, with no fresh agent-stack CVE or MCP-server compromise printing on the weaponization leg. The nearest direct signal is privacy-by-topology: Apple frames Siri's new architecture so that a roughly 3-billion-parameter on-device model handles local requests and heavier work routes to Apple Silicon servers under Private Cloud Compute - stateless, ephemeral, with personally identifying information stripped before any content reaches the Gemini inference layer rather than going to Google's own infrastructure - which is a topology-as-trust-boundary design in the same family as the attestation answer the thesis treats as structural, even though it is a privacy-engineering posture rather than signed checkpoints or per-tenant capability logs. On the structural-defense side the only movement is the forward calendar: the Confidential Computing Summit (June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint) is built around agent security, hardware-verified attestation, and attested inference, with sessions from NVIDIA, AMD, Google, Microsoft and Meta - exactly the per-tenant capability-attestation primitive vector the thesis tracks, but as a scheduled agenda rather than a shipped control, alongside the standing Black Hat AI Summit, DEF CON AI Village, and Zenity agentic-red-teaming watches. No agentic-framework CVE wave, no MCP-server quarantine telemetry, and no federal or allied procurement-enforcement datapoint landed today, so the thesis is touched only at the privacy-topology framing and a future attestation venue.

The user's second standing prediction (cloud APIs for advanced + local LLMs for daily, driven by SaaS price rises) gets its strongest direct feed in weeks, because Apple's exact topology is a clean instantiation of the advanced-cloud-plus-daily-local split the thesis names. The on-device leg is a roughly 3-billion-parameter local model that handles daily and local requests at no per-call charge, exposed to developers through the Foundation Models framework for tool-calling and structured generation precisely because the model runs locally and avoids metered API cost - the commodity-and-privacy-sensitive workloads the daily-local leg expects to settle on-device. The advanced leg routes heavier work to a custom roughly 1.2-trillion-parameter Gemini model under Private Cloud Compute, an eight-times-larger frontier system Apple chose to license rather than build because the substrate cost amortizes at frontier-lab scale - the exact advanced-workloads-stay-on-cloud-APIs dynamic the cloud leg tracks, and a striking case of even Apple concluding its in-house frontier effort had fallen a generation behind. The cost split is structural in the product itself: free local inference for daily use versus a roughly $1-billion-a-year licensed frontier tier for the heavy requests, which is the per-token-economics forcing function the thesis leans on rendered as a single shipped device architecture rather than implied, even though no fresh SaaS-API price rise or Unsloth-style local fine-tuning recipe printed alongside it.

The user's third standing prediction (RL/LLM-based forecasting performance improvement) is honestly light today, touched only with a weak governance-and-agent-surface tick and nothing on the substrate or real-world-deployment legs. The nearest signal is the agent-surface and governance frame: deeper App Intents lets the new assistant chain multi-step actions across third-party apps and the Foundation Models framework exposes the on-device model for tool-calling and guided generation, which is the kind of reusable agent-loop and tool-permission surface an autonomous forecasting agent would run on, but Apple explicitly deferred how strict the entitlements and tool-permission model will be to the June 9-12 API sessions, so the capability-gating perimeter is named but not yet specified. There is no router-only LoRA, router-aware advantage-decomposition, ultra-long-context RL-stability preprint, or signed-skill-registry interop datapoint this cycle, and the physical-AI real-world-deployment leg - the Tesla Optimus, Figure, or Foxconn production-loop cohort - prints nothing today. So the day grazes the governance leg through an agent-tool-permission surface still to be detailed, while leaving the substrate and deployment legs of the thesis untouched.
